newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq Kurd group take northern town, widen attack.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Kurd group take northern town, widen attack.

text.p: Iraqi Kurdish forces captured the northern town of Ranya early on Saturday and were moving south towards the rival stronghold of Sulaimaniya, officials of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) told Reuters.
"We took Ranya this morning and we are close to taking Quala Dizah," the official said in KDP headquarters in the town of Salahuddin, 50 miles (80 km) west of Ranya.
There were also clashes in the town of Chuman, around 40 km (25 miles) west of Iraq's border with Iran, he said.

The latest fighting between the KDP and the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) dates back to August 31, when the KDP sought help from Baghdad to recapture the main northern city of Arbil from the PUK.
Baghdad's intervention on the side of the KDP provoked U.S. cruise missile attacks on southern Iraq and a widening of the no-fly zone there.
The KDP went on to capture the whole of the three Kurdish provinces in the region but last week the PUK began a counter-assault, retaking its stronghold of Sulaimaniya and advancing back to Arbil.
A senior U.S. official was due to hold talks with KDP leader Massoud Bagzani next week -- probably in Turkey -- to try to hammer out an end to the latest conflict between the two Kurdish groups.
The KDP official said the party's peshmerga guerrillas aimed to surround Sulaimaniya by taking towns around the city and then close in for the final kill.
The capture of Ranya and attack on Chuman was part of a strategy to assault a series of positions near the Iranian border to cut off the PUK from what the KDP says are its Iranian allies.
The official said a group of KDP peshmerga was moving towards the Dukan Dam, which supplies power to Arbil and the surrounding towns.
